verses.text: After Joshua died, the Israelites asked the LORD, "Which tribe should go first to fight the Canaanites for us?"
The LORD answered, "Judah will go. Look, I have given the land into their hands."

The people of Judah said to their relatives, the people of Simeon, "Come with us into the land given to us, and let us fight the Canaanites together. Then we will go with you into your land." So Simeon went with them.
When Judah attacked, the LORD gave the Canaanites and Perizzites into their hands, and they killed ten thousand men at Bezek.
There they found Adoni-Bezek and fought against him, and they defeated the Canaanites and Perizzites.
Adoni-Bezek ran away, but they chased him, caught him, and cut off his thumbs and big toes.

Adoni-Bezek said, "Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off have picked up scraps under my table. Now God has paid me back for what I did to them." They brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
The people of Judah attacked Jerusalem and captured it. They killed its people with the sword and set the city on fire.
After that, the people of Judah went down to fight the Canaanites living in the hill country, the Negev in the south, and the western foothills.
They attacked the Canaanites living in Hebron, which used to be called Kiriath Arba, and defeated Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai.
From there they went to attack the people of Debir, which used to be called Kiriath Sepher.
Caleb said, "I will give my daughter Aksah in marriage to the man who attacks and captures Kiriath Sepher."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, captured it, so Caleb gave him his daughter Aksah as his wife.
When she came to Othniel, she urged him to ask her father for a field. When she got down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, "What would you like?"
She answered, "Do me a special favour. Since you have given me land in the dry south, give me springs of water too." So Caleb gave her the upper and lower springs.

The descendants of Moses' father-in-law, the Kenite, went up with the people of Judah from the City of Palm Trees into the Desert of Judah, in the Negev near Arad. They went and lived among the people there.
Then Judah went with their relatives from Simeon and attacked the Canaanites living in Zephath. They completely destroyed the city, so it was called Hormah, which means Destruction.
Judah also captured Gaza, Ashkelon and Ekron, each with its land around it.
The LORD was with the people of Judah. They took the hill country, but they could not drive out the people living on the plains, because they had iron chariots.
As Moses had promised, Hebron was given to Caleb, and he drove out the three sons of Anak from there.
But the people of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem. So the Jebusites still live there with the people of Benjamin today.
The descendants of Joseph attacked Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
They sent men to spy out Bethel, which used to be called Luz.
The spies saw a man coming out of the city and said to him, "Show us how to get into the city, and we will be kind to you."
So he showed them, and they killed the people of the city with the sword. But they let the man and his whole family go.
He went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a city and called it Luz. That is still its name today.
But the people of Manasseh did not drive out the people of Beth Shan, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam or Megiddo and their villages, because the Canaanites were determined to stay in that land.
When Israel became strong, they made the Canaanites do forced labour, but they never drove them out completely.
Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer, so the Canaanites kept living there among them.
Zebulun did not drive out the people living in Kitron or Nahalol. The Canaanites lived among them, but they were made to do forced labour.
Asher did not drive out the people living in Akko, Sidon, Ahlab, Akzib, Helbah, Aphek or Rehob.
So the people of Asher lived among the Canaanites of the land, because they did not drive them out.

Naphtali did not drive out the people living in Beth Shemesh or Beth Anath. They lived among the Canaanites of the land, but the people of Beth Shemesh and Beth Anath were made to do forced labour for them.
The Amorites pushed the people of Dan back into the hill country and would not let them come down to the plains.
The Amorites were determined to stay in Mount Heres, Aijalon and Shaalbim. But when the descendants of Joseph grew stronger, the Amorites were made to do forced labour.
The border of the Amorites ran from Scorpion Pass to Sela and beyond.
